hypotheses.text: Neurodevelopmental disorder with poor or absent speech, dysmorphic facies, and behavioral abnormalities (NEDSFB; OMIM #621182) exhibits dual modes of inheritance where monoallelic de novo missense variants act via dominant-negative mechanisms, whereas heterozygous loss-of-function carrier parents remain asymptomatic because simple haploinsufficiency is insufficient to cause the full syndromic phenotype.
hypotheses.rationale: The board hypothesis claimed most cases are de novo heterozygous variants acting via haploinsufficiency. However, recent cohorts show multiple consanguineous families with biallelic truncating/frameshift variants where heterozygous parents are completely healthy carriers, directly challenging haploinsufficiency as the universal mechanism and suggesting that dominant cases may involve dominant-negative or toxic effects.

evidence.text: Whole exome sequencing identified a homozygous frameshift variant (c.2604_2605delAG; p.Val870SerfsTer12) in an affected child causing significantly decreased NAV3 mRNA levels, while all carrier family members (mother, father, brother) were heterozygous and unaffected.

evidence.text: Eleven individuals from seven families harbored predicted pathogenic biallelic, de novo, and heterozygous variants in NAV3, all exhibiting intellectual disability, microcephaly, and behavioral abnormalities.

source.quote: We report eleven individuals from seven families harboring predicted pathogenic biallelic, de novo, and heterozygous variants in the NAV3 gene, which encodes the microtubule positive tip protein neuron navigator 3 (NAV3).

hypotheses.text: Biallelic NAV3 loss-of-function variants constitute the majority of confirmed clinical cases of OMIM #621182 and manifest with complete speech absence and microcephaly, whereas inherited heterozygous NAV3 missense variants produce an attenuated phenotype characterized by ambiguous or articulated speech delay without microcephaly.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifies the phenotypic divide between autosomal recessive complete-loss patients and monoallelic/heterozygous individuals, allowing clinicians to distinguish the full syndromic entity from milder neurodevelopmental speech delays.

evidence.text: To date, four homozygous and four heterozygous pathogenic variants have been reported in the literature, with a novel biallelic homozygous missense variant (c.3430T>C; p.Ser1144Pro) presenting with ambiguous speech as a distinctive finding in autosomal recessive NDD.

hypotheses.text: Pathogenic missense alterations in NAV3 specifically cluster in the conserved AAA ATPase and calponin homology (CH) domains to cause dominant-negative microtubule destabilization, whereas benign or carrier missense variants localize outside these critical domains.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolving whether missense variants act as dominant negatives or benign polymorphisms requires testing whether pathogenic variants cluster within the AAA and CH microtubule-binding domains and impair microtubule stability in vitro.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact proportion of autosomal recessive biallelic versus monoallelic de novo pathogenic NAV3 variants reported across all published probands, and do their facial dysmorphic features differ systematically?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving whether the syndrome is primarily recessive or dual-mode requires tallying every reported individual and comparing whether craniofacial dysmorphism segregates with variant zygosity.

new_directions.question_text: Does recombinant expression of monoallelic versus biallelic truncating NAV3 mutations in neuronal cell cultures demonstrate a dominant-negative effect on microtubule plus-end tracking versus simple null haploinsufficiency?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifies the biophysical mechanism explaining why heterozygous truncating carriers are healthy while heterozygous missense or de novo mutations can produce severe disease.
